audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for Sarah visitation, Isaac/laughter, weaning feast, Hagar and Ishmael wilderness episode, divine hearing, opened eyes/well, and Beersheba covenant.

verses.restored: The Eternal visited Sarah as he had said, and the Eternal did for Sarah as he had spoken.

familiar.text: And the LORD visited Sarah as he had said...

notes.title: Visited Sarah
notes.body: Paqad means visit, attend to, or act on behalf of. The promise centers Sarah directly.

modern.text: Now the LORD attended to Sarah as He had said, and the LORD did for Sarah what He had promised.

original.text: וַֽיהוָ֛ה פָּקַ֥ד אֶת שָׂרָ֖ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר אָמָ֑ר וַיַּ֧עַשׂ יְהוָ֛ה לְשָׂרָ֖ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבֵּֽר

verses.restored: Sarah conceived and bore Abraham a son in his old age, at the appointed time of which the Divine had spoken to him.

familiar.text: For Sarah conceived, and bare Abraham a son in his old age...

notes.title: Appointed time
notes.body: Isaac is born at the promised moed, the appointed time.

modern.text: So Sarah conceived and bore a son to Abraham in his old age, at the very time God had promised.

original.text: וַתַּהַר֩ וַתֵּ֨לֶד שָׂרָ֧ה לְאַבְרָהָ֛ם בֵּ֖ן לִזְקֻנָ֑יו לַמּוֹעֵ֕ד אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּ֥ר אֹת֖וֹ אֱלֹהִֽים

verses.restored: Abraham called the name of his son who was born to him, whom Sarah bore to him, Isaac.

familiar.text: And Abraham called the name of his son... Isaac.

modern.text: And Abraham gave the name Isaac to the son Sarah bore to him.

original.text: וַיִּקְרָ֨א אַבְרָהָ֜ם אֶֽת שֶׁם בְּנ֧וֹ הַנּֽוֹלַד ל֛וֹ אֲשֶׁר יָלְדָה לּ֥וֹ שָׂרָ֖ה יִצְחָֽק

verses.restored: Abraham circumcised Isaac his son when he was eight days old, as the Divine had commanded him.

familiar.text: And Abraham circumcised his son Isaac being eight days old...

modern.text: When his son Isaac was eight days old, Abraham circumcised him, as God had commanded him.

original.text: וַיָּ֤מָל אַבְרָהָם֙ אֶת יִצְחָ֣ק בְּנ֔וֹ בֶּן שְׁמֹנַ֖ת יָמִ֑ים כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה אֹת֖וֹ אֱלֹהִֽים

verses.restored: Abraham was one hundred years old when Isaac his son was born to him.

familiar.text: And Abraham was an hundred years old...

modern.text: Abraham was a hundred years old when his son Isaac was born to him.

original.text: וְאַבְרָהָ֖ם בֶּן מְאַ֣ת שָׁנָ֑ה בְּהִוָּ֣לֶד ל֔וֹ אֵ֖ת יִצְחָ֥ק בְּנֽוֹ

verses.restored: Sarah said, The Divine has made laughter for me; everyone who hears will laugh with me.

familiar.text: And Sarah said, God hath made me to laugh...

notes.title: Laughter transformed
notes.body: Earlier laughter of impossibility becomes shared laughter of fulfillment.

modern.text: Then Sarah said, “God has made me laugh, and everyone who hears of this will laugh with me.”

original.text: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר שָׂרָ֔ה צְחֹ֕ק עָ֥שָׂה לִ֖י אֱלֹהִ֑ים כָּל הַשֹּׁמֵ֖עַ יִֽצְחַק לִֽי

verses.restored: She said, Who would have said to Abraham that Sarah would nurse children? Yet I have borne a son in his old age.

familiar.text: And she said, Who would have said unto Abraham...

modern.text: She added, “Who would have told Abraham that Sarah would nurse children? Yet I have borne him a son in his old age.”

original.text: וַתֹּ֗אמֶר מִ֤י מִלֵּל֙ לְאַבְרָהָ֔ם הֵינִ֥יקָה בָנִ֖ים שָׂרָ֑ה כִּֽי יָלַ֥דְתִּי בֵ֖ן לִזְקֻנָֽיו

verses.restored: The child grew and was weaned, and Abraham made a great feast on the day Isaac was weaned.

familiar.text: And the child grew, and was weaned...

modern.text: So the child grew and was weaned, and Abraham held a great feast on the day Isaac was weaned. Sarah Turns against Hagar (Galatians 4:21–30)

original.text: וַיִּגְדַּ֥ל הַיֶּ֖לֶד וַיִּגָּמַ֑ל וַיַּ֤עַשׂ אַבְרָהָם֙ מִשְׁתֶּ֣ה גָד֔וֹל בְּי֖וֹם הִגָּמֵ֥ל אֶת יִצְחָֽק

verses.restored: Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian, whom she had borne to Abraham, laughing.

familiar.text: And Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian... mocking.

notes.title: Laughing/playing/mocking
notes.body: Metsacheq can mean laughing, playing, or mocking. The ambiguity matters because of Isaac’s laughter-name.

modern.text: But Sarah saw that the son whom Hagar the Egyptian had borne to Abraham was mocking her son,

original.text: וַתֵּ֨רֶא שָׂרָ֜ה אֶֽת בֶּן הָגָ֧ר הַמִּצְרִ֛ית אֲשֶׁר יָלְדָ֥ה לְאַבְרָהָ֖ם מְצַחֵֽק

verses.restored: She said to Abraham, Drive out this slave-woman and her son, for the son of this slave-woman shall not inherit with my son, with Isaac.

familiar.text: Wherefore she said unto Abraham, Cast out this bondwoman and her son...

notes.title: Harsh status language
notes.body: Sarah does not name Hagar or Ishmael here; the language is status-based and severe.

modern.text: and she said to Abraham, “Expel the slave woman and her son, for the slave woman’s son will never share in the inheritance with my son Isaac!”

original.text: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ לְאַבְרָהָ֔ם גָּרֵ֛שׁ הָאָמָ֥ה הַזֹּ֖את וְאֶת בְּנָ֑הּ כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יִירַשׁ֙ בֶּן הָאָמָ֣ה הַזֹּ֔את עִם בְּנִ֖י עִם יִצְחָֽק

verses.restored: The matter was very grievous in Abraham’s eyes because of his son.

familiar.text: And the thing was very grievous in Abraham's sight because of his son.

modern.text: Now this matter distressed Abraham greatly because it concerned his son Ishmael.

original.text: וַיֵּ֧רַע הַדָּבָ֛ר מְאֹ֖ד בְּעֵינֵ֣י אַבְרָהָ֑ם עַ֖ל אוֹדֹ֥ת בְּנֽוֹ

verses.restored: The Divine said to Abraham, Let it not be grievous in your eyes because of the boy and because of your slave-woman. Whatever Sarah says to you, listen to her voice, for through Isaac your seed shall be called.

familiar.text: And God said unto Abraham, Let it not be grievous in thy sight...

notes.title: Isaac and Ishmael distinguished
notes.body: The covenant line is through Isaac, while Ishmael still receives a nation-promise in the next verse.

modern.text: But God said to Abraham, “Do not be distressed about the boy and your maidservant. Listen to everything that Sarah tells you, for through Isaac your offspring will be reckoned.

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֜ים אֶל אַבְרָהָ֗ם אַל יֵרַ֤ע בְּעֵינֶ֨יךָ֙ עַל הַנַּ֣עַר וְעַל אֲמָתֶ֔ךָ כֹּל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר תֹּאמַ֥ר אֵלֶ֛יךָ שָׂרָ֖ה שְׁמַ֣ע בְּקֹלָ֑הּ כִּ֣י בְיִצְחָ֔ק יִקָּרֵ֥א לְךָ֖ זָֽרַע

verses.restored: But also the son of the slave-woman I will make into a nation, because he is your seed.

familiar.text: And also of the son of the bondwoman will I make a nation...

notes.title: Ishmael remains seed
notes.body: Ishmael is not erased from blessing; he is Abraham’s seed.

modern.text: But I will also make a nation of the slave woman’s son, because he is your offspring.”

original.text: וְגַ֥ם אֶת בֶּן הָאָמָ֖ה לְג֣וֹי אֲשִׂימֶ֑נּוּ כִּ֥י זַרְעֲךָ֖ הֽוּא

verses.restored: Abraham rose early in the morning, took bread and a skin of water, and gave them to Hagar, placing them on her shoulder, and the boy, and sent her away. She went and wandered in the wilderness of Beersheba.

familiar.text: And Abraham rose up early in the morning, and took bread, and a bottle of water...

notes.title: Sent away
notes.body: Hagar and Ishmael are expelled with limited provisions. The scene is painful and direct.

modern.text: Early in the morning, Abraham got up, took bread and a skin of water, put them on Hagar’s shoulders, and sent her away with the boy. She left and wandered in the Wilderness of Beersheba.

original.text: וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֣ם אַבְרָהָ֣ם בַּבֹּ֡קֶר וַיִּֽקַּֽח לֶחֶם֩ וְחֵ֨מַת מַ֜יִם וַיִּתֵּ֣ן אֶל הָ֠גָר שָׂ֧ם עַל שִׁכְמָ֛הּ וְאֶת הַיֶּ֖לֶד וַֽיְשַׁלְּחֶ֑הָ וַתֵּ֣לֶךְ וַתֵּ֔תַע בְּמִדְבַּ֖ר בְּאֵ֥ר שָֽׁבַע

verses.restored: The water in the skin was finished, and she placed the boy under one of the bushes.

familiar.text: And the water was spent in the bottle, and she cast the child under one of the shrubs.

modern.text: When the water in the skin was gone, she left the boy under one of the bushes.

original.text: וַיִּכְל֥וּ הַמַּ֖יִם מִן הַחֵ֑מֶת וַתַּשְׁלֵ֣ךְ אֶת הַיֶּ֔לֶד תַּ֖חַת אַחַ֥ד הַשִּׂיחִֽם

verses.restored: She went and sat opposite him at a distance, about a bowshot away, for she said, Let me not see the death of the boy. She sat opposite him, lifted her voice, and wept.

familiar.text: And she went, and sat her down over against him...

notes.title: Maternal grief
notes.body: Hagar’s grief is foregrounded before divine hearing.

modern.text: Then she went off and sat down nearby, about a bowshot away, for she said, “I cannot bear to watch the boy die!” And as she sat nearby, she lifted up her voice and wept.

original.text: וַתֵּלֶךְ֩ וַתֵּ֨שֶׁב לָ֜הּ מִנֶּ֗גֶד הַרְחֵק֙ כִּמְטַחֲוֵ֣י קֶ֔שֶׁת כִּ֣י אָֽמְרָ֔ה אַל אֶרְאֶ֖ה בְּמ֣וֹת הַיָּ֑לֶד וַתֵּ֣שֶׁב מִנֶּ֔גֶד וַתִּשָּׂ֥א אֶת קֹלָ֖הּ וַתֵּֽבְךְּ

verses.restored: The Divine heard the voice of the boy, and the messenger of the Divine called to Hagar from the heavens and said to her, What is with you, Hagar? Do not fear, for the Divine has heard the voice of the boy where he is.

familiar.text: And God heard the voice of the lad...

notes.title: God hears
notes.body: Ishmael’s name means God hears, and the wilderness scene repeats that theme.

modern.text: Then God heard the voice of the boy, and the angel of God called to Hagar from heaven, “What is wrong, Hagar? Do not be afraid, for God has heard the voice of the boy where he lies.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֣ע אֱלֹהִים֮ אֶת ק֣וֹל הַנַּעַר֒ וַיִּקְרָא֩ מַלְאַ֨ךְ אֱלֹהִ֤ים אֶל הָגָר֙ מִן הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַיֹּ֥אמֶר לָ֖הּ מַה לָּ֣ךְ הָגָ֑ר אַל תִּ֣ירְאִ֔י כִּֽי שָׁמַ֧ע אֱלֹהִ֛ים אֶל ק֥וֹל הַנַּ֖עַר בַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר הוּא שָֽׁם

verses.restored: Rise, lift up the boy and hold him with your hand, for I will make him into a great nation.

familiar.text: Arise, lift up the lad...

modern.text: Get up, lift up the boy, and take him by the hand, for I will make him into a great nation.”

original.text: ק֚וּמִי שְׂאִ֣י אֶת הַנַּ֔עַר וְהַחֲזִ֥יקִי אֶת יָדֵ֖ךְ בּ֑וֹ כִּֽי לְג֥וֹי גָּד֖וֹל אֲשִׂימֶֽנּוּ

verses.restored: The Divine opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water. She went, filled the skin with water, and gave the boy a drink.

familiar.text: And God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water...

modern.text: Then God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water. So she went and filled the skin with water and gave the boy a drink.

original.text: וַיִּפְקַ֤ח אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶת עֵינֶ֔יהָ וַתֵּ֖רֶא בְּאֵ֣ר מָ֑יִם וַתֵּ֜לֶךְ וַתְּמַלֵּ֤א אֶת הַחֵ֨מֶת֙ מַ֔יִם וַתַּ֖שְׁקְ אֶת הַנָּֽעַר

verses.restored: The Divine was with the boy, and he grew. He dwelled in the wilderness and became an archer.

familiar.text: And God was with the lad; and he grew...

modern.text: And God was with the boy, and he grew up and settled in the wilderness and became a great archer.

original.text: וַיְהִ֧י אֱלֹהִ֛ים אֶת הַנַּ֖עַר וַיִּגְדָּ֑ל וַיֵּ֨שֶׁב֙ בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר וַיְהִ֖י רֹבֶ֥ה קַשָּֽׁת

verses.restored: He dwelled in the wilderness of Paran, and his mother took a woman for him from the land of Egypt.

familiar.text: And he dwelt in the wilderness of Paran...

modern.text: And while he was dwelling in the Wilderness of Paran, his mother got a wife for him from the land of Egypt. The Covenant at Beersheba

original.text: וַיֵּ֖שֶׁב בְּמִדְבַּ֣ר פָּארָ֑ן וַתִּֽקַּֽח ל֥וֹ אִמּ֛וֹ אִשָּׁ֖ה מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם

verses.restored: At that time Abimelech, with Phicol commander of his army, said to Abraham, The Divine is with you in all that you do.

familiar.text: And it came to pass at that time, that Abimelech and Phichol...

modern.text: At that time Abimelech and Phicol the commander of his army said to Abraham, “God is with you in all that you do.

original.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֔וא וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲבִימֶ֗לֶךְ וּפִיכֹל֙ שַׂר צְבָא֔וֹ אֶל אַבְרָהָ֖ם לֵאמֹ֑ר אֱלֹהִ֣ים עִמְּךָ֔ בְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר אַתָּ֖ה עֹשֶֽׂה

verses.restored: Now swear to me here by the Divine that you will not deal falsely with me, with my offspring, or with my descendants. According to the kindness I have done with you, you shall do with me and with the land in which you have sojourned.

familiar.text: Now therefore swear unto me here by God that thou wilt not deal falsely...

modern.text: Now, therefore, swear to me here before God that you will not deal falsely with me or my children or descendants. Show to me and to the country in which you reside the same kindness that I have shown to you.”

original.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה הִשָּׁ֨בְעָה לִּ֤י בֵֽאלֹהִים֙ הֵ֔נָּה אִם תִּשְׁקֹ֣ר לִ֔י וּלְנִינִ֖י וּלְנֶכְדִּ֑י כַּחֶ֜סֶד אֲשֶׁר עָשִׂ֤יתִי עִמְּךָ֙ תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה עִמָּדִ֔י וְעִם הָאָ֖רֶץ אֲשֶׁר גַּ֥רְתָּה בָּֽהּ

verses.restored: Abraham said, I swear.

familiar.text: And Abraham said, I will swear.

modern.text: And Abraham replied, “I swear it.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אַבְרָהָ֔ם אָנֹכִ֖י אִשָּׁבֵֽעַ

verses.restored: Abraham reproved Abimelech because of a well of water that Abimelech’s servants had seized.

familiar.text: And Abraham reproved Abimelech because of a well of water...

modern.text: But when Abraham complained to Abimelech about a well that Abimelech’s servants had seized,

original.text: וְהוֹכִ֥חַ אַבְרָהָ֖ם אֶת אֲבִימֶ֑לֶךְ עַל אֹדוֹת֙ בְּאֵ֣ר הַמַּ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֥ר גָּזְל֖וּ עַבְדֵ֥י אֲבִימֶֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: Abimelech said, I do not know who has done this thing. You did not tell me, and I had not heard of it until today.

familiar.text: And Abimelech said, I wot not who hath done this thing...

modern.text: Abimelech replied, “I do not know who has done this. You did not tell me, so I have not heard about it until today.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲבִימֶ֔לֶךְ לֹ֣א יָדַ֔עְתִּי מִ֥י עָשָׂ֖ה אֶת הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וְגַם אַתָּ֞ה לֹא הִגַּ֣דְתָּ לִּ֗י וְגַ֧ם אָנֹכִ֛י לֹ֥א שָׁמַ֖עְתִּי בִּלְתִּ֥י הַיּֽוֹם

verses.restored: Abraham took sheep and cattle and gave them to Abimelech, and the two of them cut a covenant.

familiar.text: And Abraham took sheep and oxen, and gave them unto Abimelech...

modern.text: So Abraham brought sheep and cattle and gave them to Abimelech, and the two men made a covenant.

original.text: וַיִּקַּ֤ח אַבְרָהָם֙ צֹ֣אן וּבָקָ֔ר וַיִּתֵּ֖ן לַאֲבִימֶ֑לֶךְ וַיִּכְרְת֥וּ שְׁנֵיהֶ֖ם בְּרִֽית

verses.restored: Abraham set seven ewe-lambs of the flock by themselves.

familiar.text: And Abraham set seven ewe lambs of the flock by themselves.

modern.text: Abraham separated seven ewe lambs from the flock,

original.text: וַיַּצֵּ֣ב אַבְרָהָ֗ם אֶת שֶׁ֛בַע כִּבְשֹׂ֥ת הַצֹּ֖אן לְבַדְּהֶֽן

verses.restored: Abimelech said to Abraham, What are these seven ewe-lambs that you have set by themselves?

familiar.text: And Abimelech said unto Abraham, What mean these seven ewe lambs...

modern.text: and Abimelech asked him, “Why have you set apart these seven ewe lambs?”

original.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֲבִימֶ֖לֶךְ אֶל אַבְרָהָ֑ם מָ֣ה הֵ֗נָּה שֶׁ֤בַע כְּבָשֹׂת֙ הָאֵ֔לֶּה אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִצַּ֖בְתָּ לְבַדָּֽנָה

verses.restored: He said, You shall take these seven ewe-lambs from my hand, so that it may be a witness for me that I dug this well.

familiar.text: And he said, For these seven ewe lambs shalt thou take of my hand...

modern.text: He replied, “You are to accept the seven ewe lambs from my hand as my witness that I dug this well.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר כִּ֚י אֶת שֶׁ֣בַע כְּבָשֹׂ֔ת תִּקַּ֖ח מִיָּדִ֑י בַּעֲבוּר֙ תִּֽהְיֶה לִּ֣י לְעֵדָ֔ה כִּ֥י חָפַ֖רְתִּי אֶת הַבְּאֵ֥ר הַזֹּֽאת

verses.restored: Therefore he called that place Beersheba, because there the two of them swore an oath.

familiar.text: Wherefore he called that place Beersheba; because there they sware...

notes.title: Beersheba
notes.body: The name plays on well, seven, and oath.

modern.text: So that place was called Beersheba, because it was there that the two of them swore an oath.

original.text: עַל כֵּ֗ן קָרָ֛א לַמָּק֥וֹם הַה֖וּא בְּאֵ֣ר שָׁ֑בַע כִּ֛י שָׁ֥ם נִשְׁבְּע֖וּ שְׁנֵיהֶֽם

verses.restored: They cut a covenant at Beersheba. Then Abimelech and Phicol commander of his army rose and returned to the land of the Philistines.

familiar.text: Thus they made a covenant at Beersheba...

modern.text: After they had made the covenant at Beersheba, Abimelech and Phicol the commander of his army got up and returned to the land of the Philistines.

original.text: וַיִּכְרְת֥וּ בְרִ֖ית בִּבְאֵ֣ר שָׁ֑בַע וַיָּ֣קָם אֲבִימֶ֗לֶךְ וּפִיכֹל֙ שַׂר צְבָא֔וֹ וַיָּשֻׁ֖בוּ אֶל אֶ֥רֶץ פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים

verses.restored: Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beersheba and called there on the name of the Eternal, El Olam, God of the Age/Forever.

familiar.text: And Abraham planted a grove in Beersheba, and called there on the name...

notes.title: El Olam
notes.body: El Olam can mean Everlasting God or God of the Age. The title is preserved with gloss.

modern.text: And Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beersheba, and there he called upon the name of the LORD, the Eternal God.

original.text: וַיִּטַּ֥ע אֶ֖שֶׁל בִּבְאֵ֣ר שָׁ֑בַע וַיִּ֨קְרָא שָׁ֔ם בְּשֵׁ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה אֵ֥ל עוֹלָֽם

verses.restored: Abraham sojourned in the land of the Philistines many days.

familiar.text: And Abraham sojourned in the Philistines' land many days.

modern.text: And Abraham resided in the land of the Philistines for a long time.

original.text: וַיָּ֧גָר אַבְרָהָ֛ם בְּאֶ֥רֶץ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים יָמִ֥ים רַבִּֽים
